definition: A phenomenon where gradients grow uncontrollably large during backpropagation, destabilizing training.
details: Exploding gradients are commonly addressed with gradient clipping, careful initialization, and normalization layers.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Boil it down and it is this: A phenomenon where gradients grow uncontrollably large during backpropagation, destabilizing training. Here is why it matters: Exploding gradients are commonly addressed with gradient clipping, careful initialization, and normalization layers. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Exploding Gradient Problem.
